title: Algerian eye stitch panel
subtitle: A framed panel of five Algerian eye stars with tent stitch fill on 13-count canvas
excerpt: Five Algerian eye stitches arranged in a quincunx pattern (four at the corners, one at the centre) make a traditional eyelet panel. The radiating stitches to the centre hole give each motif a small opening at its heart. Finished size is 12 by 12 cm.
sourceNotes: Algerian eye stitch layout from Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), eyelet stitch chapter. Quincunx arrangement synthesised from geometric canvaswork examples in Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882).

glossaryTerms.definition: An arrangement of five elements: one at each corner and one in the centre: like the five on a die. A common motif layout in both embroidery and quilting.

heroPrompt: A small framed needlepoint panel showing five Algerian eye star eyelets in gold on cream, arranged in a quincunx, showing the open centre holes of each eyelet, natural light.

content.text: Five Algerian eye stitches in a
quincunx

arrangement make a quiet, precise panel. Each Algerian eye uses eight stitches radiating from the outer corners of a 4 by 4 hole square to a shared centre hole. Drawing all threads through the same centre hole opens a small eyelet. The design area is 62 by 62 holes on 13-count canvas, finishing at 12 by 12 cm.
What you need

items.label: Canvas
items.value: 13-count mono canvas, cut 22 by 22 cm (leaves a 5 cm margin around the 62 by 62 hole design area)

items.label: Thread: eye stars
items.value: Stranded cotton, 3 strands. Suggested: DMC 729 / Anchor 890 (medium old gold). About 5 m. Use a fine thread to keep the centre hole open

items.label: Thread: background
items.value: Persian wool, 1 strand. Suggested: DMC 712 / Anchor 926 (cream). About 8 m

items.label: Thread: border
items.value: Persian wool, 1 strand. Suggested: DMC 838 / Anchor 1088 (very dark beige brown). About 3 m

items.label: Needle
items.value: Tapestry size 22 (fine enough for the eyelet technique)

content.text: Palette
Eye stars: DMC 729 / Anchor 890: medium old gold (stranded cotton, 3 strands)
Background: DMC 712 / Anchor 926: cream (Persian wool, 1 strand)
Border: DMC 838 / Anchor 1088: very dark beige brown (Persian wool, 1 strand)
Stretching the canvas
Mount on a small hoop or frame. The eyelet stitches draw the canvas threads together at the centre hole; a taut canvas helps keep the background area flat around the eyelets.
Stitches used
Algerian eye stitch
: 8 stitches from the 8 points of the outer square to the shared centre hole
Basketweave tent stitch
: background and border
Working method

Mark the five eyelet positions on the canvas. The centre eyelet sits at hole 31 by 31. The four corner eyelets sit at holes 13 by 13, 13 by 49, 49 by 13, and 49 by 49. Each eyelet occupies a 4 by 4 hole square.

Work the five eyelets. For each eyelet, bring the thread up at one of the eight outer points and down through the centre hole. Pull each stitch firmly but not so hard the canvas distorts. Work all 8 stitches of the eyelet before moving on.
Work the two-hole border in the dark shade using tent stitch.
Fill the cream background in basketweave, working around the eyelet areas carefully.
Block by pressing under a damp cloth and a book for two hours.
Finishing
Lace over the 12 by 12 cm mounting board and frame in a narrow border frame.
What to try next
A grid of Algerian eyes in one colour, with no gaps between eyelets, makes a fully textured ground. Use it as a fill for a box lid or small cushion.
